notes: Adversarial prompt linter. Grade both what it catches AND what it correctly leaves alone — a linter that flags everything is worthless. Cases 1–4 and 7 are true positives (a specific rule must fire at its severity); cases 5 and 6 are calibration controls (a rule must NOT fire — safety prohibitions are not R4 steering-negatives; a clean outcome-oriented prompt must not be gutted). Case 8 exercises the requires_tier dependency (no model named → call model-recommender first). Every fired finding must cite the rule_id + severity from prompt-audit-rules.md and be accompanied by a rewritten prompt. Rule ids/severities are those in prompt-audit-rules.md as of 2026-07-05.

evals.name: deliberation-railroaded-R1
evals.prompt: Audit this prompt (target: opus). Prompt: 'Design our caching layer. Step 1: add a Redis client. Step 2: wrap every DB call. Step 3: set TTL 60s. Step 4: return the cached value.'
assertions: Fires R1-archetype-mismatch at severity block: a deliberation task scripted as step-by-step edits, throttling the judgment you want
Rewrite converts it to goal + acceptance criteria + constraints with the HOW left open
Does not praise before reporting the finding

evals.name: execution-open-ended-R1
evals.prompt: Audit this prompt (target: sonnet). Prompt: 'Improve the auth module.'
assertions: Fires R1-archetype-mismatch at severity block: an execution task left open-ended — no scope, acceptance, or verification
Also flags R5-unstated-expectations (implicit scope/output) as warn
Rewrite adds tight scope + explicit acceptance + a verification command

evals.name: fable-reasoning-echo-R3
evals.prompt: Audit this prompt (target: fable). Prompt: 'Solve the problem and show your full chain of thought — transcribe all your reasoning step by step in the response before the answer.'
assertions: Fires R3-reasoning-echo-trap at severity block (target is Fable)
Explains the risk: can trigger the reasoning_extraction refusal and silently fall back to Opus 4.8
Rewrite removes the show-your-reasoning instruction and suggests reading adaptive thinking blocks / a progress channel instead

evals.name: negatives-to-positives-R4
evals.prompt: Audit this prompt. Prompt: 'Write the release notes. Don't be verbose. Don't use markdown. Avoid jargon.'
assertions: Fires R4-negatives-to-positives at severity warn on the 'don't/avoid' steering instructions
Rewrite states the positive behavior (e.g. 'write 3–5 flowing prose sentences in plain language')
Does not escalate a warn to block

evals.name: prohibitions-not-flagged-control
evals.prompt: Audit this prompt (target: sonnet). Prompt: 'Implement the fix in a worktree and open a PR. Never force-push, never merge, and never deploy — a human does that. Done when `make test` exits 0.'
assertions: Does NOT fire R4 on 'never force-push/merge/deploy' — these are safety prohibitions, not steering negatives
Recognizes the prompt as well-formed execution (scope + verification present)
Emits few or no findings and does not rewrite it wholesale

evals.name: clean-prompt-not-gutted-control
evals.prompt: Audit this prompt (target: sonnet). Prompt: 'In parsers/, add null-guards to every parse* function that lacks one (goal). Done when: no parse* dereferences input without a guard, and `npm test` passes. Don't change the public signatures. Here is one example of the guard style: <example>if (!raw) return null;</example>'
assertions: Recognizes it as a well-scoped execution prompt (explicit scope, acceptance, verification, and an example)
Emits at most 1–2 minor findings; does not gut or wholesale-rewrite it
If it flags 'Don't change the public signatures' it is at most a nit (borderline prohibition), not a block

evals.name: review-literal-filtering-R10
evals.prompt: Audit this prompt (target: opus). Prompt: 'Review this PR. Only report high-severity bugs and don't nitpick.'
assertions: Fires R10-review-literal-filtering at severity warn
Explains that a literal-following model obeys 'only high-severity' at the finding stage, dropping measured recall
Rewrite asks for full coverage with confidence + severity, moving filtering to a downstream step

evals.name: requires-tier-dependency-no-model
evals.prompt: Audit this prompt (no target model given): 'Refactor the billing service to be faster.'
assertions: Because no model is named, calls model-recommender to resolve the task's archetype → tier before evaluating requires_tier rules
Then audits against that tier's profile (execution vs deliberation posture)
Fires R1/R5 (open-ended, no scope/acceptance) and rewrites with scope + verification
